Article Title: Delhi Police serves notice to X over 'derogatory' posts targeting constitutional heads
Article Text:
Delhi police wrote to X seeking removal of 'abusive' posts about Constitutional hads

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Wednesday wrote to social media platform X, formerly Twitter, seeking the removal of content allegedly containing "derogatory, malicious and defamatory content" targeting constitutional authorities.In its notice, the police asked the platform to "immediately delete/remove" the alleged post or video and furnish complete registrant details of the X account that uploaded the content, including the user's full name, address, contact number and email ID.The police also sought the account's login and logout details, along with corresponding timestamps, and any other information that could assist the investigation.Additionally, X has been asked to preserve all data related to the post or video for the ongoing probe and provide a certificate under Section 63(4) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA).The latest notice comes days after Delhi Police directed multiple social media platforms to remove posts and videos containing offensive and abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi that were allegedly uploaded during the student protests at Jantar Mantar and the violence linked to the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' march.According to police, abusive posts targeting the Prime Minister surfaced across several social media platforms during the protests and subsequent clashes in the national capital.Officials said the Delhi Police's social media monitoring team has been continuously scanning online platforms for objectionable content. Whenever such posts are identified, notices are issued to the concerned social media intermediaries directing them to remove the content.Police said several posts and videos containing abusive language directed at the Prime Minister have already been taken down following such notices.The monitoring exercise is continuing, with cyber and social media teams maintaining surveillance of online activity linked to the protests to identify additional content that may violate applicable rules.The developments come amid heightened political tensions following the July 20 'Chalo Sansad' march, during which students protesting alleged irregularities in the NEET and CBSE examinations clashed with security personnel while marching from Jantar Mantar towards Parliament.
Article Summary: Delhi police wrote to X seeking removal of 'abusive' posts about Constitutional hads. Police asked platform to "immediately delete/remove" the alleged post or video. The latest notice comes days after Delhi Police directed multiple social media platforms to remove posts and videos against Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Article Title: NEET-UG leak probe: CBI gets 3 more days to file annexures in chargesheet, hearing on August 3
Article Text: NEW DELHI: A special fast-track court at Rouse Avenue on Wednesday listed the CBI's chargesheet in the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case for consideration on August 3 and granted the agency three more days to file the remaining annexures.The court was informed that the CBI had filed a chargesheet running into around 20,000 pages against 13 accused. The agency sought additional time to file the annexures, witness statements and the list of documents, saying the records were being scanned before being supplied to the accused, according to ANI.Special fast track court Judge Anu Grover Baliga allowed the request and granted the CBI three days to complete the filing.During the hearing, the court noted that the chargesheet submitted on Tuesday was not accompanied by witness statements or the list of documents. The CBI told the court that the records were voluminous and would be filed within three days.Deputy Legal Advisor A P Singh, Senior Public Prosecutor V K Pathak and Public Prosecutor Arjun Anand appeared for the CBI during the hearing.Earlier on Tuesday, the CBI filed a chargesheet against 13 accused, including three National Testing Agency (NTA) subject experts, two coaching centre associates, middlemen and several beneficiary candidates.The agency invoked charges of criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust and destruction of evidence under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024."The CBI cited 360 witnesses, 422 documents and 43 material objects in this charge sheet. All 13 chargesheeted persons are in judicial custody as on date," the agency's spokesperson had said.The CBI said it had attached digital forensic analysis reports, handwriting expert opinions and academic experts' assessments of the leaked question paper."These reports confirmed the role of the accused in circulation of leaked questions prior to the date of examination," the spokesperson said.The agency took over the probe on May 12 after the Department of Higher Education lodged a complaint over alleged irregularities and a paper leak in the NEET-UG 2026 examination held on May 3. The examination was later cancelled and a re-examination was conducted on June 21.According to the CBI, its two-month investigation traced the alleged conspiracy from the source of the paper leak to the beneficiary candidates, identifying the entire chain involved. The agency also said it had tracked the money trail and frozen several bank accounts, bank lockers and a demat account linked to the accused.Among those named in the chargesheet are three arrested NTA subject experts, PV Kulkarni (Chemistry), Manisha Gurunath Mandhare (Biology) and Manisha Sanjay Havaldar (Physics).Also named are Latur-based doctor Manoj Shirure, Tejas Harshadkumar Shah, a physics faculty member at Pune-based Dr Abhang Prabhu Medical Academy (APMA), and Shivraj Raghunath Motegaonkar of a coaching centre in Latur.
Article Summary: The court was informed that the CBI had filed a chargesheet running into around 20,000 pages against 13 accused. The agency sought additional time to file the annexures, witness statements and the list of documents. Judge Anu Grover Baliga allowed the request and granted the CBI three days to complete the filing.

Article Title: India slams POK elections, Pakistan's claims over Indus Valley legacy
Article Text:
MEA slams Pakistan

India slammed Pakistan for the Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK) polls, saying the "cosmetic electoral exercise" was just an attempt to camouflage the illegal occupation of Indian territory.Ministry of external affairs (MEA) reiterated India's "consistent, clear and well known" position that the entire Union territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, including the areas currently under Pakistan's illegal and forcible occupation, are integral and inalienable parts of India."We have seen reports regarding the so-called legislative assembly elections being conducted in POK...the current cosmetic electoral exercise is nothing but an attempt by Pakistan to camouflage its illegal occupation and hide its grave human rights violations in the region," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.Asked about Pakistan's efforts to reclaim the Indus Valley Civilisation legacy, the official again cited Pakistan's backing of terrorism, saying a country which has been promoting cross-border terrorism, religious fundamentalism and violence for decades, cannot have any claim to any pluralistic cultural legacy.
Article Summary: India slammed Pakistan for the Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK) polls. India said the "cosmetic electoral exercise" was just an attempt to camouflage the illegal occupation of Indian territory. MEA reiterated India's "consistent, clear and well known" position that Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh are integral and inalienable parts of India.

Article Title: Ahmedabad tragedy: Supreme Court accepts pilot dad's plea not to make Air India crash report public
Article Text:
SG Mehta said the government will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to the SC in a sealed cover

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Tuesday accepted the request of the father of the pilot, who died in the Ahmedabad air crash last June, for not making public the final inquiry report, expected in Oct, and the Centre said that it will furnish the report in a sealed cover to the court.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that govt respects the sentiments of the pilot's father and will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to Supreme Court in a sealed cover. The SG, however, brushed aside objections to the ongoing inquiry into the crash of Air India's London flight that killed 260, all but one passenger and many on ground.Appearing for the NGO, advocate Prashant Bhushan attempted to punch holes in the inquiry, terming it to be biased because of absence of independent members in the probe team and said it did not follow the standard operating procedure for such inquiries. The solicitor general said the inquiry is being conducted following prescribed process scrupulously.Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) on July 14 had responded to the petition filed by the deceased pilot's father Pushkar Raj Sabharwal, and said, "In view of the nature, scale and complexity of the present accident, the AAIB has carefully assessed the timeline for completion of the investigation.In all probability, the investigation activities, subject to resolution of the pending external dependencies, are anticipated to be completed within six weeks. ""Thereafter, the draft final report, following completion of the analysis phase, is expected to be ready approximately in Oct 2026," it had said. "As per the treaty mandate, upon preparation of draft final report, the same has to be mandatorily shared with the Accredited Representatives of the State of Design and Manufacture, for comments, as required under the relevant rules of International Civil Aviation Organisation , which in the present case - the National Transportation Safety Board, USA. "
Article Summary: Supreme Court accepts request of the father of the pilot, who died in the Ahmedabad air crash last June. Centre said that it will furnish the report in a sealed cover to the court. SG Tushar Mehta said the government will submit the final report, as soon as it is finalised, to the SC.

Article Title: NEET protest: All SOPs followed, pellet gun use on protesters authorised, reveals CRPF review
Article Text:
File photo: July 20 NEET protest march

‘Police, RAF attacked with stones, iron rails’

NEW DELHI: All standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters, which included the authorised use of "non-lethal" means like pellet gun, a CRPF post-event analysis has said.CRPF sources told TOI that upon carefully examining the response of its anti-riot unit, Rapid Action Force, it is evident that force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed to effectively control the mob. Around 3-5 protesters were injured by the metal pellets. Also, 47 RAF personnel were injured, with six sustaining head injuries.When contacted, CRPF DG G P Singh said the matter was "sub judice" and any findings or view of the force on RAF action would be placed before Supreme Court. RAF sources said the use of force on July 20 was authorised by Delhi Police, in line with the SOPs and the law.Sources claimed the mob had some motivated elements attacking personnel of Delhi Police and RAF with stones and, in some cases, even iron rails.As per BNSS, an executive magistrate may order use of civil force to disperse an unlawful assembly after carefully assessing the situation.In Delhi, this magisterial authority is vested with the Delhi Police commissioner, and delegated to junior commissioners till the level of the assistant commissioner of police. “RAF deployed at protest sites uses anti-riot gear only with authorisation; which in this case came from the DCP/ACP in charge of the protest site. Such authorisation is in writing and as per a format used at all sites of unlawful assembly; no order is given verbally,” said an officer.CRPF sources said pump action guns are an approved, “non-lethal” measure to control unlawful assemblies. “Their use, with the force gradient being followed and under authorisation by the competent officer, is as per the SOP,” said an officer.J&K high court had, in its 2016 ruling on a PIL challenging pellet use, said: “So long as there is violence by unruly mobs, use of force is inevitable. What kind of force has to be used at the relevant point of time or in a given situation has to be decided by the persons in charge of the place where the attack is happening. This court in writ jurisdiction, without any finding rendered by the competent forum/authority cannot decide whether the use of force in a particular incident is excessive or not. ”Supreme Court later dismissed the special leave petition against this order, stating, “The use of pellet guns, if at all done by any agency, has not only not been barred, but validated through these orders.”
Article Summary: All standard operating procedures (SOPs) and anti-riot drills were followed during the July 20 police action against anti-NEET leak protesters. CRPF sources said force gradient was followed, with pump action gun being used only after lower-grade measures like public announcements for crowd dispersal, tear gas and lathicharge failed.

Article Title: Centre may table bill to make deepfakes, digital arrest separate offences
Article Text:
Digital arrest (representative image)

NEW DELHI: Government on Tuesday said it may introduce a bill in the ongoing session of Parliament making digital arrest and AI-generated deepfakes a distinct offence, after Supreme Court pointed out that existing penal laws do not define these offences.Solicitor General (SG) Tushar Mehta said the law will be aimed at categorising digital arrest and AI-generated deepfakes as specific offences with consequential punishments.During suo motu proceedings on the mechanism to curb the menace of digital arrest, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said SC has taken a harsh stand against those involved in digital arrest scams and denied them bail, but asked do penal laws define such offences?“You (govt) may need to formally define the case of digital arrest in penal laws,” the bench told attorney general R Venkataramani.“It (digital arrest) has elements of extortion, robbery and organised crime. Do you need to define this as a standalone offence with stringent consequences like freezing of assets of accused persons?” the bench asked attorney general R Venkataramani, who has been coordinating with a high-level inter-departmental committee constituted especially for dealing with the menace of digital arrest.Justice Bagchi said coming up with a law designed to deal with digital scams is a job that govt alone can do.“We now have deepfakes which can be used for misleading people or can be used for cheating and impersonation. Using our (exclusive) powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, we can neither define a crime nor create a new offence,” he said.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta told the bench that he has been consulted on this issue by govt and it is likely to introduce a relevant bill in the present session of Parliament. Venkataramani said because of a coordinated action facilitated by the inter-departmental committee, incidents of digital arrest have recorded a drastic fall. He said the panel is in the process of finalising a comprehensive report to identify gaps in the system and measures to plug them.Supreme Court after taking suo motu cognizance of spiralling incidents of digital arrest, especially targeting retired people and robbing them of their life’s savings, had tasked CBI to probe incidents being reported from across the country.Appearing for WhatsApp, senior advocate Kapil Sibal told SC that the social media platform is coordinating with govt to stop misuse of the platform for commission of crime.
Article Summary: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the law will be aimed at categorising digital arrest and AI-generated deepfakes as specific offences. Supreme Court pointed out that existing penal laws do not define these offences. Justice Bagchi said coming up with a law designed to deal with digital scams is a job that govt alone can do.

Article Title: 'I regret it': Mehbooba Mufti claims Jantar Mantar remark a slip of tongue, apologises
Article Text:
File photo: PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti

SRINAGAR: Under fire for her Jantar Mantar remark that appeared to justify the use of force in Kashmir on grounds of “militancy”, PDP president Mehbooba Mufti Tuesday apologised, but claimed it was a slip of tongue and accused governing NC and chief minister Omar Abdullah of deliberately misinterpreting her comment.“If my words have hurt or upset my people, who consider me one of their own and often hold me accountable even over small matters, then I sincerely apologise,” Mehbooba said. “If they have been hurt by my statement, I regret it.”Explaining the controversial remark, she said: “One clip from my interaction, in which I used the word ‘banta hai’ (understandable) while referring to militancy, went viral. I said that in haste. The remark was interpreted differently.”While talking to reporters at Jantar Mantar on July 23 during the CJP protest, Mehbooba is heard saying in a widely circulated video: “We have seen this (use of force against protesters) for the first time in Delhi. We have witnessed it in Kashmir for many years. Magar wahan militancy hai, uska ek banta hai (But militancy exists there, so it is understandable).”With Omar lapping up the remark and accusing her of supporting the repression of Kashmiris, the former J&K chief minister clarified she meant to say ‘bahana’ (excuse) banta hai, but in a slip of tongue, said “banta hai”.“The video circulating is genuine, but the meaning being attributed to my words is not,” she said.NC, however, rejected her apology and clarification. “The only appropriate response is a clear and unconditional apology to every Kashmiri who was hurt, especially the victims of pellet injuries,” party spokesperson Tanvir Sadiq said.“Also, apologise for your alliance with BJP and for bringing them to power in Jammu & Kashmir. Everything else said today was simply an attempt to divert attention from your original remarks,” he added.
Article Summary: Mehbooba Mufti apologises for her Jantar Mantar remark that appeared to justify the use of force in Kashmir on grounds of "militancy" PDP president claims it was a slip of tongue and accused governing NC and chief minister Omar Abdullah of deliberately misinterpreting her comment.

Article Title: July 20 NEET protest: SC asks states to release student protesters under 18 with no criminal records
Article Text:
"Whosoever committed excesses, took law in their hands should be taken to task," SC observed.

ALSO READ |

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed Delhi and all state governments to release all arrested or detained protesters under the age of 18 with no criminal antecedents and ordered the police to preserve all digital evidence.The court also noted that a fair and independent probe into all allegations of "police excesses against protesting NEET students" was required. The top court's observations come as the opposition continues to protest the use of pellet guns against demonstrators marching towards Parliament on July 20."Whosoever committed excesses, took law in their hands should be taken to task", the court ovserved as per news agency PTI, adding: "Once there is violation of defined protocol, law must take care of it."The top court said a prima facie case had been made out for a transparent inquiry by a commission and added that the exercise should help frame a protocol for handling such situations in the future.The hearing also brought before the court allegations of police excesses from several states, including claims that a police officer in Bihar used an AK-47 against peaceful protesters.The Supreme Court also sought responses by Monday from states where incidents of violence were reported during the student protests.The apex court further directed the authorities to preserve digital records collected through CCTV cameras, facial recognition systems and drones. It ordered that such material, as well as the personal data of protesters, must not be placed in the public domain.Senior advocate Prashant Bhushan separately referred to a petition filed on behalf of protest volunteer Junaid Malik, alleging that he and his family were assaulted by the police.Taking note of the submissions, Chief Justice Surya Kant said the material placed before the court suggested there were allegations that warranted closer examination."If we start looking at individual facts… the most conservative language we can use is that there is, prima facie, a case of violence involved. That’s why we are hearing these matters."Appearing for the central government and the Delhi Police, solicitor general Tushar Mehta said the petitioners had accused the police of using excessive force during the protests and maintained that any wrongdoing by the police must be dealt with."If that is the case, they must be punished and action must be taken."At the same time, Mehta told the court that more than 250 police personnel had also sustained injuries during the protests."There is one truth, another truth, and then there is The truth, which this Court needs to examine."The chief justice observed that the allegations of attacks on police personnel also required investigation and sought clarity on who was responsible."For these attacks on police officials, the issue also needs to be addressed. Is it done by students or by…?"Responding to the query, Mehta said the authorities did not believe the students had attacked the police. He submitted that the violence may have been carried out by miscreants or "uninvited guests" who had infiltrated the protest.Justice Joymalya Bagchi also cautioned against attributing violence to an entire movement, observing, "There are always people discrediting a peaceful crowd."
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders release of all arrested or detained protesters with no criminal antecedents. The court also ordered the police to preserve all digital evidence. The top court's observations come as the opposition continues to protest the use of pellet guns against demonstrators.

Article Title: Gandhi siblings vs Pralhad Joshi: 'Defender of rapists' charge meets 'authenticate it' challenge
Article Text:
Pralhad Joshi; Priyanka Gandhi Vadra

NEW DELHI: Congress MPs Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi of appointing as the new education minister a leader who had "expressed happiness over the release of those who raped a pregnant woman. "Union minister Pralhad Joshi has been given additional charge of the ministry of education following the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25 amid nationwide student protests over the NEET (UG) paper leak.Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was the first to target Joshi, making the remarks during the Lok Sabha debate on the Centre's proposed amendments to the anti-paper leak law."The prime minister appointed a new education minister, a person who expressed consent and even happiness over the release of those convicted of raping a pregnant woman," the Wayanad MP alleged, prompting Union minister Pralhad Joshi and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to intervene and demand that she substantiate the claim.An irate Joshi demanded that Priyanka Gandhi Vadra be expelled from the House and asked her to apologise for the remark.However, she hit back saying that has a video of the minister backing the convicted rapists."At a time when they are saying that they are bringing in women's rights, women's reservations and they are putting women in the forefront...It's a very wrong message...I am going to authenticate. There is a video of that time.I will submit everything with proper procedure," Priyanka Gandhi Vadra stated.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi backed his sister and remarked that there cannot a "filthier" person than one who defends release of convicted rapists."Education minister of India - the BJP puts a man who is a defender of rapists. That is the most filthy type of man. There can be no flithier man than somebody who says that rapists need protection. That is the education minister of India today. It's a strange reaction from the PM, that there are so many people in his cabinet, he could have chosen anyone of them. But he chooses a person who protects rapists. Quite amazing!," Rahul Gandhi told reporters.The siblings appeared to be referring to the case of Bilkis Bano, who was gang-raped during the 2002 Gujarat riots. The 11 convicts were released in August 2022, triggering widespread outrage, before the Supreme Court quashed their release in January 2024.Speaking to a news channel in October 2022, Joshi had said the convicts' release was in accordance with the law.
Article Summary: Congress MPs Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Rahul Gandhi target education minister Pralhad Joshi. Joshi has been given additional charge of the ministry of education following the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25 amid nationwide student protests over NEET (UG) paper leak.

Article Title: Jammu and Kashmir: Army duo hurt in Uri accidental blast
Article Text:
File photo: Army personnel near LoC

SRINAGAR: Two Army jawans were injured in an accidental blast near the Line of Control in J&K’s Uri sector, a Srinagar-based defence spokesperson stated Tuesday.The blast occurred in Uri’s Kamalkote area, Lt Col M K Sahu said, adding that the duo was rushed to the Army’s Base Hospital at Badamibagh, Srinagar, for treatment.“They are both stable. There is no threat to life,” Sahu said.
Article Summary: The blast occurred in Uri’s Kamalkote area, Lt Col M K Sahu said. The duo was rushed to the Army”s Base Hospital at Badamibagh, Srinagar, for treatment. “They are both stable. There is no threat to life,” Sahu added.

Article Title: ‘It hurts to remember’: Blind since 14, J&K pellet survivor searches for tomorrow
Article Text:
As NEET protests spur crowd control debate, Kashmir’s scars resurface

Insha Mushtaq has been blind since 14

SEDOW(SHOPIAN): Behind a mesh screen, Insha Mushtaq sits in a mustard headscarf, offering a faint smile. She cannot see the camera or the daylight filtering through her window. She only senses. Ten years after pellets took her eyes during J&K’s 2016 unrest, she still carries scars that have become public property, resurfacing every time India debates crowd control.She wishes they wouldn’t. “I don’t want to remember. It doesn’t help and it hurts,” said the 24-year-old, seated inside her home in Sedow village of Shopian, about 75km south of Srinagar.Yet memory has a stubborn half-life. Images of 14-year-old Insha, her face wrapped in bandages after being struck by pellets during protests following Hizbul Mujahideen commander Burhan Wani’s killing, travelled across TV screens and social media in 2016. They turned her into perhaps J&K’s most recognisable face of pellet gun wounds. Every fresh political quarrel over use of force drags those photographs back into public view.Recent protests over NEET irregularities in New Delhi have done exactly that.For Insha, the debate translates into reopening wounds she has spent years trying to close. “I don’t know whether I should talk or not. I want to do a job after completing my education,” she said, her father Mushtaq Ahmad Lone and mother Afroza Akhtar sitting quietly beside her.She has not abandoned her future. Blindness altered her life, not her ambition. She is completing a bachelor’s degree in arts and hopes to find a govt job under disability quota. Speaking publicly, she fears, could jeopardise that dream.“I don’t know what happened in Delhi but I know many lives were destroyed by pellet guns in Kashmir,” she said. Then her face brightened. “I am blind but we can operate phones.”Pellet guns entered J&K’s security arsenal around 2010 as a supposedly non-lethal alternative to bullets. They left behind hundreds of eye wounds, partial blindness and permanent loss of vision. Years dulled national attention, but memories never disappeared. Protests in New Delhi breathed fresh life into an old controversy.Political sparring has followed. Governing National Conference has accused opposition Peoples Democratic Party of condemning pellet guns in New Delhi while defending their use in J&K. PDP, in turn, has blamed CM Omar Abdullah for introducing pellet guns during his earlier tenure to tackle protests after about 110 demonstrators were killed in security action during 2009-10.According to BJP, use of bullets and pellets ceased after Article 370’s abrogation in 2019 because protests largely ended.Former J&K DGP SP Vaid, who headed police during 2016 unrest, said pellet guns were first used during 2009-10 protests and again in 2016. “All those 110 people killed in 2010 died due to bullets not pellets. Pellet gun should be used only as a last resort, from a proper distance and aimed below the waist,” Vaid said.Describing them as 12-bore pump-action guns, he said: “I’m not saying pellet guns are good. I am saying they are a better last-resort option than direct firing with live ammunition. If the choice is between bullets and pellet guns, pellet guns can save lives.”Politics feels distant inside Insha’s two-storey home. She now climbs stairs unaided. Certificates marking completion of classes 11 and 12 line her room. But July 12, 2016 remains etched with painful clarity.Clashes had broken out outside her home. Tear gas shells landed nearby. Curious, she walked to a window overlooking the village road. The instant she opened it, a volley of pellets shattered glass and ripped into her face. “My forehead felt like it was burning from inside,” she said.She was taken first to Shopian district hospital before doctors referred her to Shri Maharaja Hari Singh Hospital in Srinagar. She slipped into a coma for 4 days.Her photographs quickly became emblematic of 2016 unrest, prompting intervention by then PDP-BJP govt. Then CM Mehbooba Mufti promised assistance — gave Insha’s father a job. After spending nearly a month at SMHS Hospital, Insha was shifted to AIIMS New Delhi, where she remained for almost 2 months.On Sept 13, 2016, she was moved to Aditya Jyot Eye Hospital in Mumbai, where ophthalmologist Dr S Natarajan treated her for nearly 24 days. Natarajan, then hospital director and president of Ocular Trauma Society of India, operated on hundreds of pellet survivors during repeated visits to J&K that year.Doctors eventually told her family she had no perception of light. Blindness would be lifelong.An intervention proved transformative. “Nadir Ali helped me continue my education. He kept insisting that I should study. Had he not been there, I would have been finished,” Insha said.Ali, chairperson of J&K Centre for Peace and Justice Foundation, first met her in late 2017. “She was not born blind. She was angry, very angry and undergoing surgeries regularly for removal of pellets,” he said.Ali admitted her to special education department at Delhi Public School in Srinagar, where she spent nearly 2 years learning Braille, mobility skills and computer applications. “When I visited her home, I saw people had given her certificates but no one seemed to be thinking about how she would build a future,” he said. “She wanted to study and I wanted to help her. She had to learn how to walk independently, use a computer and adapt to a completely new way of life. ”Today, Insha studies political science, English, education and sociology through Ignou. Graduation is within reach. “This is her final year… Our aim is to make her financially independent,” Ali said.Ali has another appeal, one directed at journalists: “Once you tell them to recount their past, they again slip into trauma. Let them heal.” For Insha, that may be hardest of all. The country remembers a photograph. She lives its aftermath.
Article Summary: Insha Mushtaq has been blind since 14 after being struck by pellets during protests following Burhan Wani's killing. Images of 14-year-old Insha, her face wrapped in bandages, travelled across TV screens and social media in 2016. Every fresh political quarrel over use of force drags those photographs back into public view.

Article Title: Jammu and Kashmir: Bus with Amarnath pilgrims slips into gorge, 39 hurt
Article Text:
Security personnel gather near the wreckage after a bus carrying Amarnath Yatra pilgrims skids off the road and plunged into a gorge

SRINAGAR: At least 39 Amarnath pilgrims, including 21 from Madhya Pradesh and 19 Rajasthan natives, were injured after their bus skidded off the road in Ganiwan in J&K’s Ganderbal district and slipped into a 50-foot-deep gorge on Tuesday morning. The fall was broken midway at around 25 feet by a house in a mountain hamlet below the road, preventing the vehicle from sliding further down the slope and averting a major tragedy, locals said.The devotees were heading back after visiting the holy cave shrine. The vehicle was moving from Baltal towards Srinagar when the accident occurred around 7 am near Ranga Morh, prompting a multi-agency rescue operation. Residents said the house belonged to Din Mohammad, who was away grazing sheep with his family at the time.J&K Police, CRPF, ITBP, health department and civil defence personnel rushed to the spot and launched a coordinated rescue operation, with assistance from locals. The injured were moved to SKIMS in Soura, Srinagar.J&K Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha visited SKIMS, where doctors briefed him about the health condition of those injured. In an X post, Sinha said he instructed officials to ensure the best possible treatment for the hospitalised pilgrims and arrangements for their safe return upon recovery.Health minister Sakeena Itoo also visited SKIMS and interacted with the injured pilgrims, assuring them of full govt support. She directed hospital authorities to monitor each patient’s condition and ensure round-the-clock availability of specialist doctors and essential healthcare services.This year's Amarnath Yatra began on July 3. The 57-day annual pilgrimage will conclude on Aug 28, coinciding with Raksha Bandhan. As of July 26, more than 4,14,000 pilgrims had completed the annual pilgrimage and offered prayers at the holy cave shrine.
Article Summary: At least 39 Amarnath pilgrims, including 21 from Madhya Pradesh and 19 Rajasthan natives, were injured after their bus skidded off the road. The fall was broken midway at around 25 feet by a house in a mountain hamlet below the road, preventing the vehicle from sliding further down the slope. The devotees were heading back after visiting the holy cave shrine.

Article Title: After SC order, West Bengal govt says no action against NEET protesters, except those with criminal records
Article Text:
A protest over the NEET paper leak issue, in Kolkata, West Bengal. (PTI photo)

NEW DELHI: The West Bengal government on Tuesday announced that it would not take any coercive action against students who participated in recent demonstrations over the NEET (UG) paper leak issue.However, the BJP-led state government clarified that the relief would not apply to individuals with criminal antecedents.The directions are in line with the Supreme Court's interim order earlier in the day, under which states can continue investigations into registered FIRs but cannot take coercive action against students who participated in protests, provided they have no criminal antecedents.According to an official press release, one case had been registered in West Bengal in connection with the NEET (UG) paper leak protest issue and 16 people had been arrested as of 6 pm on July 26.Earlier, two other BJP-led states, Bihar and Assam, announced the withdrawal of cases and legal proceedings against all protesters involved in demonstrations over the alleged NEET (UG) examination irregularities.In Maharashtra, another BJP-led state, chief minister Devendra Fadnavis directed the state home department to issue orders for the withdrawal of cases registered against students who participated in the protests.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), an online satirical outfit that led the main protests in Delhi, has warned of resuming its agitation if cases against all protesters are not withdrawn. The demand was among the conditions accepted by the Centre, following which the CJP called off its indefinite sit-in on July 25.The CJP had been protesting at Delhi's Jantar Mantar since June 21.
Article Summary: West Bengal government says it will not take coercive action against protesters. However, relief would not apply to individuals with criminal antecedents. Two other BJP-led states, Bihar and Assam, announced withdrawal of cases. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has warned of resuming its agitation if cases are not withdrawn.

Article Title: 13 Indians stranded aboard vessel in Ukraine amid repeated drone, missile attacks: Report
Article Text:
13 Indian seafarers trapped in vessel in Ukraine amid repeated drone, missile attacks

NEW DELHI: Thirteen Indian seafarers are among 15 crew members stranded on board a cargo vessel at Ukraine's Chornomorsk port, where repeated drone and missile attacks have placed the crew in what has been described as a "life-threatening situation", according to the Forward Seamen's Union of India (FSUI).In an urgent appeal posted on X, the union said the vessel, MV AMIR1, remains docked at Chornomorsk while hostilities continue in the surrounding area."MV AMIR1, currently at Ukrainian port Chornomorsk with 15 crew on board, including 13 Indian seafarers, is trapped in a terrible and life-threatening situation," it said.The union alleged that drone and missile attacks were being carried out in the immediate vicinity of the ship, leaving the crew in constant fear."Repeated drone and missile attacks are being attempted in the immediate vicinity of the vessel. The crew is living under constant fear of a direct hit at any moment," it said.The FSUI urged the shipowners, the vessel's flag state, the relevant authorities and the government to intervene immediately to ensure the crew's safety and facilitate their evacuation."We urgently appeal to all concerned authorities, shipowners, flag state, and the Government of India to immediately secure their safety and arrange prompt repatriation," the union said.Calling for urgent action, it added, "Indian seafarers must not be left as sitting targets in conflict zones. Act now."This comes a day after MEA raised concerns with Ukraine over the safety of Indian seafarers in the Black Sea. On Monday, the MEA summoned Ukraine's ambassador to India, Dr Oleksandr Polishchuk, following an attack on the merchant vessel MV OMORFI near the Ukrainian port of Odesa that had four Indian crew members on board.The MEA said the strike resulted in the death of an Indian national and condemned attacks on commercial shipping in the "strongest terms", calling them a threat to maritime safety, freedom of navigation and international commerce. It also urged Kyiv to ensure that commercial vessels carrying civilian seafarers are not targeted.
Article Summary: Thirteen Indian seafarers are among 15 crew members stranded on board a cargo vessel at Ukraine's Chornomorsk port. Repeated drone and missile attacks have placed the crew in what has been described as a "life-threatening situation", according to the Forward Seamen's Union of India.

Article Title: Delhi Police officer denies authorising alleged RAF pellet gun firing during CJP march: Report
Article Text:
RAF troops deployed at Jantar Mantar during now-called off CJP protest

NEW DELHI: A senior Delhi Police officer has denied being present at the spot when a Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel allegedly fired from a pellet gun at protesters during the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) Parliament march on July 20, officials said on Tuesday.A General Diary (GD) entry recorded by the Rapid Action Force (RAF) at Parliament Street police station mentions that the officer was present in Zone-1 near Jantar Mantar when the alleged incident took place, PTI reported.The officer, however, claimed that he was nearly half a kilometre away from the spot when the pellet rounds were reportedly fired.Meanwhile, a high-level meeting was held at the Delhi Police headquarters on Tuesday to discuss the GD entry related to the alleged use of non-lethal munitions, including plastic pellets, by the RAF, the specialised riot-control wing of the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF).Attended by senior Delhi Police officers, the meeting focused on the circumstances surrounding the GD entry recorded on July 22 at 1:24 pm.According to official police records, the GD entry was made ased on information provided by a Deputy Commandant-rank RAF officer. It states that RAF personnel deployed in Zone-1 alongside a Deputy Commissioner of Police-rank Delhi Police officer fired multiple non-lethal munitions after received rmission from the senior police officer.According to the entry, the RAF fired 55 non-electrical shells, 15 electrical shells, five tear smoke grenades, two rounds from anti-riot guns and two rounds of plastic pellets while controlling the crowd.Officials said one round of plastic pellets contains four plastic projectiles, which differ from metal pellets and are designed to cause less serious injuries.The alleged use of plastic pellets has become a major political flashpoint after reports that some protesters sustained grievous pellet injuries during the violence. Multiple Delhi Police, RAF and CRPF personnel were also injured in the clashes.Delhi Police has maintained that allegations of the force using pellet guns against protesters are "false and misleading", reiterating its position in a statement on its official X handle. According to the police, more than 65 protesters and over 200 police personnel were injured during the clashes.
Article Summary: A senior Delhi Police officer has denied being present at the spot when a Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel allegedly fired from a pellet gun at protesters. A General Diary (GD) entry recorded by the RAF mentions that the officer was present in Zone-1 near Jantar Mantar when the alleged incident took place. The officer, however, claimed that he was nearly half a kilometre away from the spot.

Article Title: Don't damage water bodies under garb of beautification: SC warns Bihar government
Article Text:
Don't damage water bodies under garb of beautification, SC to Bihar government

TOI report on Darbhanga ponds

NEW DELHI: Taking a stern view of allegations that the Bihar government is filling parts of three historic ponds in Darbhanga to create public amenities such as recreation spaces and stalls, the Supreme Court on Tuesday warned the state govt “not to touch the water bodies under the garb of beautification” without its approval.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed the state govt to immediately stall the ongoing work related to the ‘Beautification and Rejuvenation of Gangasagar, Digghi and Harahi Lake’ project. Although the state refuted the allegations of encroachment and urged the court to allow the work to continue, describing it as an ambitious project worth more than ₹100 crore, the bench refused to budge and ordered that no further work be carried out.“You cannot fill up water bodies under the garb of beautification. Do not touch the water ponds, keep your hands off and tell your officers not to touch the ponds,” the bench told advocate Manish Kumar, who was appearing for the state government.TOI had reported on July 13, with photographs, that three ponds in Darbhanga were being filled with soil and boulders to make way for stalls and footpaths, despite strong opposition from local residents and environmentalists.Advocate Renu Prajapati, appearing for the Darbhanga-based voluntary group Talab Bachao Abhiyan (TBA), informed the bench that the three ponds form part of a list of protected wetlands and that any construction on their banks would violate rules and earlier rulings of the apex court. She also pointed out that the state, in its own affidavit, had admitted that around four acres of the ponds would be filled under the project.In its affidavit, the state claimed that no arbitrary filling of the water bodies was taking place and that the activity was highly restricted and meticulously planned “Earth Filling & Stone Pitching” work.“This process is a necessity to stabilise and strengthen the severely eroded embankments, directly executing the mandate of the NGT’s order. Furthermore, the soil-filling footprint is strictly limited — for instance, constituting exactly 1.00 acre out of the 37.73-acre Harahi site, 1.42 acres out of the 50.97 acres at Digghi Lake, and 1.69 acres out of 44.22 acres at Gangasagar Lake,” the affidavit stated.After a brief hearing, the bench directed the government to stop the work and ensure that the area of the ponds remain intact and is not reduced by filling..Justifying the project, the state said the integration of public amenities is aimed at managing footfall, ensuring public hygiene, and preventing future degradation.The court was hearing a plea filed by retired academicians, environmentalists and concerned citizens under the banner of TBA. They are seeking urgent intervention to halt the filling of three historic ponds in Darbhanga — all 800–900 years old and integral to the city’s identity.“Since the State is acting in contravention of these orders and having been left with no other remedy, the petitioner herein is constrained to approach this court seeking an urgent and immediate remedy to stop further filling of the ponds and further to remove all the encroachments in and around the three ponds of Darbhanga and restore those to their original position as depicted in the maps of the years 1868 and 1960,” the petition stated.In its response, the state submitted: “It is respectfully submitted that in order to tackle the unregulated access which historically led to the lakes becoming open garbage dumps, the project provides structured and safe public utility interfaces including the construction of 11 designated bathing ghats equipped with 5 changing rooms and 7 sanitary toilet blocks to eliminate open defecation and water contamination. ”
Article Summary: Bihar government is filling parts of three historic ponds in Darbhanga to create public amenities such as recreation spaces and stalls. Supreme Court on Tuesday warned the state govt “not to touch the water bodies under the garb of beautification” without its approval.

Article Title: As Maldives president seeks SAARC summit, India says cooperation requires goodwill
Article Text:
Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu

With Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu calling for resumption of the biennial SAARC summit process, India reiterated Tuesday that it's Pakistan's support for cross-border terrorism that has blocked the intergovernmental organisation, which was conceived to build a connected and integrated South Asia. Muizzu in his Independence Day speech had also offered to act as a mediator between India and Pakistan to advance talks for an early leaders' summit.The last SAARC summit was held in 2014 in Nepal. The next summit that Pakistan was scheduled to host in 2016 could never take place as India pulled out because of the cross-border Uri terrorist attack. India has since maintained that regional cooperation under SAARC is adversely affected due to continued support to cross-border terrorism and interference in the internal affairs of member-states by Pakistan.Member-states like the Maldives, Bangladesh and Nepal have from time-to-time sought revival of the summit. "India favors strong regional cooperation and has been working towards it for several decades. Everyone in South Asia is aware of which country and what activities are responsible for stymieing SAARC," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, adding that cooperation requires goodwill.The official was responding to a question about Muizzu's remarks in which he had sought "reactivation' of SAARC calling it vital for regional peace and security."We must bring matters to the point where the leaders of SAARC resume holding summits once again," said Muizzu."To those parties among whom differences have arisen in this regard, the Maldives calls upon you to set those matters aside, to prioritise friendship for the sake of regional development and regional peace, and to come to the negotiating table. Should the task prove challenging, the Maldives stands ready to take the initiative and act as a mediator to advance those discussions," said the president, adding that SAARC must be operationalised once again and that his administration would always champion peace.Muizzu also said that SAARC had brought numerous benefits to the region"However, we now witness a span of some nine years during which this organisation has been rendered, or has become, dysfunctional. Given that the foreign policy of the Maldives is structured...upon the principle that differences should be addressed through consultation, by bringing concerns to the discussion table, reaching resolutions, and moving forward in a manner that benefits all, the reactivation of SAARC is equally vital for regional peace and security," he added.Muizzu said his government's foreign policy was based on the conviction that if differences are left to be settled by violence and force, no resolution will ever be found.
Article Summary: Maldives President Mohamed Muizzu called for resumption of the biennial SAARC summit process. India reiterated Tuesday that it's Pakistan's support for cross- border terrorism that has blocked the intergovernmental organisation. The last SAARC Summit was held in 2014 in Nepal.

Article Title: Demand for MSP, reforms: Protesting farmers breach police barricades enroute to Bhopal
Article Text:
Farmers march from Narmadapuram to Bhopal (ANI image)

Farmers marching from Narmadapuram to Bhopal demanding 100 per cent procurement of moong at the Minimum Support Price (MSP) breached police barricades on Tuesday as they entered the Madhya Pradesh capital, intensifying their protest against the state government.Visuals from Bhopal showed farmers crossing police barricades while carrying the Tricolour. Police did not use force and eventually opened the route, allowing the farmers to proceed into the city.The protest, organised under the banner of the Samyukta Kisan Morcha, began on Monday with a sit-in at Sethanighat in Narmadapuram, where farmers recited the Hanuman Chalisa before starting their march towards Bhopal, PTI reported.Earlier, police had attempted to stop the march by erecting barricades at Bhopal Tiraha and other locations. District Magistrate Somesh Mishra and Superintendent of Police Saikrishna S. Thota held talks with the protesting farmers on National Highway-69, but the discussions failed to break the deadlock.The farmers are demanding 100 per cent procurement of moong under MSP, a solution to issues related to the e-token system, and the timely availability of fertilisers at reasonable prices.
Article Summary: Farmers march from Narmadapuram to Bhopal demanding 100 per cent procurement of moong at the Minimum Support Price (MSP) They breached police barricades on Tuesday as they entered the Madhya Pradesh capital, intensifying their protest. Police did not use force and eventually opened the route, allowing the farmers to proceed into the city.

Article Title: 'Clock it', 'delulu': How Gen Z lingo took over Parliament during anti-paper leak Bill debate
Article Text:
Parliament debates anti-paper leak Bill

'Clock it'

NDA MP's 'delulu' jibe at opposition

Priyanka's swipe at PM's videos

NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 on Tuesday wasn't just about examination reforms and paper leaks. It also turned into an unexpected showcase of Gen Z vocabulary, with MPs across party lines dropping terms such as "clock it", "MIA", "FOMO" and "delulu" to sharpen their political arguments.From the treasury benches praising the Centre's reforms to the opposition attacking the government's handling of the NEET controversy, lawmakers reached for internet slang more commonly found on social media than in Parliament.BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj used the Gen Z phrase "clock it" — a slang term used to recognise something — while backing the proposed legislation.Speaking in favour of the Bill, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution."Calling the amendment a "transformative" step, Swaraj argued that it reflected the government's commitment to protecting the integrity of public examinations."I am standing in support of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. This is a transformative amendment. Its necessity is not only evident, but it is also the demand of the present time. Bringing this amendment is proof of the sensitivity of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his committed government.Speaker Sir, when a competitive examination is compromised, its impact is not limited to the candidate whose future is put at stake," she added.Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Lata Eknath Shinde turned to multiple Gen Z expressions to mock the opposition's protests over the NEET paper leak."I'd like to sum up the opposition's protest in Gen Z language. They were MIA (missing in action) for the first 37 days and did not go to Jantar Mantar. Then came FOMO (fear of missing out), so they held a protest outside the Prime Minister's residence. Finally, they became 'delulu' (delusional), believing the protesting students would join them—but no one did," Shinde said.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, meanwhile, invoked Gen Z while targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public outreach, arguing that young people could see through political messaging."If you want to win over the Gen Z, then making videos with different camera angles will not help. The prime minister needs to change the angle of his heart, not the angle of cameras," she said.She also urged the government to acknowledge the concerns raised by students over the examination controversy."Injustice has been done with youths under your government, accept the truth. Prime Minister Narendra Modi must take responsibility," Priyanka said.The Lok Sabha began discussing the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill at 2pm on Tuesday. Union Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said leaders from several parties, including the Congress, Samajwadi Party, DMK and NCP, had agreed to extend the debate from the originally scheduled six hours to eight hours.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha debate on exam reforms turned into showcase of Gen Z vocabulary. MPs across party lines dropped terms such as "MIA", "FOMO" and "delulu" to sharpen their arguments. Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra invoked Gen Z while targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public outreach.
