Article Title: 'His personal thoughts': RSS distances itself from Kerala right-wing activist over Delhi student protest remarks
Article Text:
Right-wing political commentator TG Mohandas (File photo)

NEW DELHI: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) on Tuesday distanced itself from right-wing political commentator TG Mohandas over his remarks on the recent student protests in Delhi, clarifying that he does not hold any position in the organisation.Senior RSS functionary KB Sreekumar said Mohandas was not an office-bearer of the RSS at any level and described his remarks as "personal thoughts", adding that the comments deserved to be condemned."TG Mohandas's comments on the recent protest are his personal thoughts. He is not an RSS official at any level. RSS doesn't agree with his views and they should be condemned in every highest possible manner," Sreekumar told PTI.The clarification came a day after Mohandas's remarks triggered widespread protests in Kerala and sparked outrage on social media, prompting the CPI-backed All India Students' Federation (AISF) to file a police complaint against him.In its complaint to the Kerala DGP, the AISF alleged that Mohandas had called for student protesters to be "shot dead", amounting to an appeal for violence and mass killing.According to the complaint, publicly advocating the use of state force to open fire on protesting students, with the possibility of deaths and grievous injuries, was an extremely dangerous statement that promoted violence, undermined the value of human life and had the potential to create fear and social unrest.The student outfit sought registration of a criminal case against Mohandas under all applicable legal provisions and urged an investigation into the YouTube channel that carried the remarks, the source of the video, related digital records and its circulation across social media platforms.The controversy stems from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar over the NEET (UG) paper leak and broader education reforms.The satirical online platform launched its indefinite agitation on June 21 and called it off on July 25 after then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the Centre accepted all three of its demands, one of which was Pradhan's resignation or ouster.The RSS, which has now distanced itself from Mohandas's remarks, is the ideological mentor of the BJP , the party leading the government at the Centre.
Article Summary: Right-wing political commentator TG Mohandas has sparked outrage with his remarks on the recent student protests in Delhi. The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) has distanced itself from his remarks. Senior RSS functionary KB Sreekumar described his remarks as "personal thoughts", adding that the comments deserved to be condemned.

Article Title: 'Garlanded as if he won a war': Opposition attacks BJP over Dharmendra Pradhan's felicitation after resignation
Article Text:
Opposition attacks BJP over Dharmendra Pradhan's felicitation after resignation

What opposition said

NEW DELHI: A political row erupted in Parliament on Tuesday after the BJP's public felicitation of former Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, who resigned over the NEET-UG paper leak controversy, drew sharp criticism from the Opposition.Congress leaders accused the ruling party of celebrating a minister who resigned amid one of the country's biggest examination crises, saying he was welcomed "as if he were a superstar" and "had returned from a war against Pakistan".The controversy stems from Monday's scenes at the Parliament complex, where BJP and NDA MPs welcomed Pradhan with chants of "Dharmendra Pradhan zindabad", draped him in a traditional stole and cap, and escorted him into the House in a show of solidarity just two days after his resignation.Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra led the opposition's attack, calling it "shameful" that BJP MPs welcomed Pradhan in Parliament despite his resignation over the alleged NEET paper leak controversy."Don't you think it is shameful? Everyone saw the circumstances under which Dharmendra Pradhan resigned, but yesterday in the Parliament premises, he was welcomed as if he were a superstar!" she said.She also accused the government of continuing to target students despite the controversy."No one can trust the Modi government, because even today, students are being harassed. I saw some Instagram handles with photographs of women alleging that they did such and such thing...Do you want to engage in talks to resolve this matter or you are still after the students, wanting to suppress them? This is wrong," Priyanka Gandhi said.Speaking during the debate on the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026 in the Lok Sabha, Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi echoed the criticism, saying Pradhan had been welcomed "as if he had returned from a war against Pakistan.""...21 children lost their lives; they committed suicide. The minister under whose watch 21 children lost their lives, when he resigned from his post and returned to the House yesterday, you garlanded him as if he had returned from a war against Pakistan," Gogoi said.The BJP's show of solidarity came after Pradhan resigned on Saturday following sustained protests over the alleged NEET paper leak. He has since been replaced by Union minister Prahlad Joshi.Meanwhile, the government has announced a series of measures to overhaul the examination system, including a high-powered task force headed by Nandan Nilekani, proposed amendments to the anti-paper leak law, and fast-track courts to deal with examination fraud cases.
Article Summary: Congress leaders accuse ruling party of celebrating a minister who resigned amid one of the country's biggest examination crises. Opposition: Dharmendra Pradhan was welcomed "as if he were a superstar" and "had returned from a war against Pakistan" The controversy stems from Monday's scenes at the Parliament complex, where BJP and NDA MPs welcomed him.

Article Title: 'Cosmetic exercise to camouflage illegal occupation': MEA rejects Pak-organised polls in PoK
Article Text:
MEA rejects Pak-organised polls in PoK

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Tuesday dismissed the legislative assembly elections being held in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK), calling the exercise a "cosmetic" attempt by Islamabad to legitimise its "illegal occupation" of the region.Responding to reports on the polls, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated that the entire Union territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh, including areas currently under Pakistan's control, are an integral part of India."We have seen reports regarding the so-called legislative assembly elections being conducted in the Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir... The entire union territories of Jammu, Kashmir and Ladakh, including the areas currently under illegal and forcible occupation of Pakistan, are integral parts of India," he said."The current cosmetic electoral exercise is nothing but an attempt by Pakistan to camouflage its illegal occupation and hide its grave human rights violations in the region. The ongoing mass protest in the Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir is the direct consequence of its economic exploitation, its denial of fundamental rights to the people and its administrative oppression," he added.PoK has been gripped by sustained protests for nearly two months, with demonstrators accusing the Pakistani authorities of political repression, economic exploitation and denying basic rights.The unrest has now begun to overshadow the region's legislative assembly elections, prompting the postponement of polling in two constituencies and drawing criticism from international rights groups.The latest escalation came on Monday when thousands of protesters marched towards Muzaffarabad after talks between the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC) and the authorities collapsed, marking the 52nd day of the agitation.The protest movement is being spearheaded by the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), which says it is fighting for greater political freedoms, economic relief and an end to what it describes as administrative oppression by Pakistani authorities.
Article Summary: The ministry of external affairs dismissed the legislative assembly elections being held in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK) PoK has been gripped by sustained protests for nearly two months, with demonstrators accusing the Pakistani authorities of political repression, economic exploitation and denying basic rights.

Article Title: 'Milestone legislation' vs 'Pradhan saved Pradhan Mantri': Centre, Oppn clash as Lok Sabha debates new anti-paper leak bill - top developments
Article Text:
Lok Sabha is discussing the amendment to the anti-paper leak law

Bill reaffirms govt's commitment to safeguard students' welfare: Jitendra Singh



Cong condemns Delhi Police action on protesters



Pradhan's removal saved 'Pradhan Mantri': Akhilesh Yadav



PM Modi 'clocked it': BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj invokes 'Gen Z language'



Bill can't erase 12 years of incompetence: Abhishek Banerjee



Priyanka Gandhi Vadra attacks Centre



Gandhis vs Pralhad Joshi



NEW DELHI: The Lok Sabha on Tuesday took up for discussion the Centre's proposed legislation to amend the anti-paper leak law, amid nationwide calls for tougher safeguards against examination fraud and wider education reforms following the NEET (UG) question paper leak in May.Union minister Jitendra Singh introduced the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, on Monday after the first week of Parliament's Monsoon session, which began on July 20, was washed out amid large-scale student protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The demonstrations ultimately forced Dharmendra Pradhan to resign as education minister.No discussion on the Bill could take place during the first six days of the Monsoon session as the opposition remained firm on its demand for a government response to the police action against student protesters in the national capital and several other parts of the country.Following Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, Union minister Pralhad Joshi has been assigned additional charge of the Ministry of Education.Opening the debate, Union minister Jitendra Singh described the proposed legislation as a "reaffirmation" of the government's commitment to protecting students' interests.Singh said the Bill seeks to amend the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, which he described as the first legislation of its kind in independent India."The earlier Act and the amendment today are, in a way, a reaffirmation of this government's deep commitment to safeguard the welfare of the students and the youth of this country," he said.Calling it a "milestone legislation", Singh added that the Bill also reflected Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resolve "not to allow anyone to compromise with the future of the children of Mother India."Opening the debate for the opposition, Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi criticised the BJP for garlanding former education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, alleging that 21 students had died by suicide after the NEET (UG) examination was cancelled following the question paper leak.Pradhan, was welcomed by MPs of the BJP-led NDA with garlands when he arrived in Parliament on Monday, two days after stepping down."21 children lost their lives; they committed suicide. The minister under whose watch 21 children lost their lives, when he resigned from his post and returned to the House yesterday, you garlanded him as if he had returned from a war against Pakistan," Gogoi remarked.Gogoi also took a jibe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi over the Instagram reels he released for student protesters, saying the government had prioritised messaging over meaningful education reforms."Today, the Prime Minister appears in Instagram reels. In the first Cabinet meeting, instead of having a comprehensive discussion on how to improve education and dismantle the paper-setting mafia, paper-solving mafia and the testing centre mafia, Prime Minister Modi simply said to focus more on Instagram," Gogoi added.He also sought an explanation from the government over the alleged use of tear gas, pellet guns and lathi-charge against student protesters, including women."Who ordered the use of tear gas, pellet guns, lathi-charge and assault on women? We want answers," the Jorhat MPSamajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also took a swipe at the BJP over Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, saying the removal of "Pradhan" had saved the "Pradhan Mantri" (prime minister)."Imagine the immense relief the members must have felt and the major crisis from which they were saved. By removing one 'Pradhan', you effectively saved the 'Pradhan Mantri'," Yadav remarked, in a jibe at the government.Yadav also raised the issue of the alleged theft of donations at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya, questioning the BJP-led Uttar Pradesh government's ability to prevent paper leaks.Referring to the alleged incident, the SP chief asked how those who had failed to prevent the theft of devotees' offerings could be expected to stop question paper leaks.Yadav also described the CJP-led demonstrations as the first student agitation in which parents of the protesting students also participated.Speaking in favour of the Bill during the debate, BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution.""I am standing in support of the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026. This is a transformative amendment. Its necessity is not only evident, but it is also the demand of the present time. Bringing this amendment is proof of the sensitivity of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his committed government. Speaker Sir, when a competitive examination is compromised, its impact is not limited to the candidate whose future is put at stake," she added.Abhishek Banerjee of the Mamata Banerjee-led Trinamool Congress (TMC) faction backed the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, but said supporting the legislation did not amount to endorsing the Centre's handling of paper leaks. Stressing that students deserved fair examinations, he said, "Support for this bill cannot be a substitute for accountability."Banerjee argued that "a stronger law is necessary, yes, but by itself is not sufficient" if examinations continue to be undermined by systemic failures. He also described the amendment as "an admission that the NDA and the BJP government have failed" to protect the integrity of public examinations, adding that "increasing punishment would erase 12 years of incompetence."Taking a swipe at the government, he alleged that "whenever governance fails, they change the law; whenever administration collapses, they increase punishment," asserting that "governance is not done by headlines; governance is measured by outcomes."Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra accused the BJP-led Centre of "hollowing" out the education system by filling it with "RSS pracharaks". She also criticised the creation of the National Testing Agency (NTA), alleging that the government had centralised the examination system while reducing the share of the education budget.The Wayanad MP also questioned the use of force against student protesters, asking, "What was the need to unleash pellet guns and AK-47s on the country's youth? Were they terrorists?" Demanding accountability, she asked who had ordered the use of pellet guns and whether the decision was taken by the Prime Minister or the Home Minister.The Siwan district administration in Bihar later clarified that the use of an AK-47 during the protests was unauthorised and inappropriate for public crowd-control duties, and that the constable concerned had been suspended.Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also recalled meeting the mother of a student who was injured during police action and admitted to the ICU at a Delhi hospital. She said the mother was distressed by repeated visits from politicians, telling them, "Even those who are responsible for my daughter's condition came here. Why?" Calling the encounter deeply moving, the Congress leader appealed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah to explain "what was the need to inflict such oppression on an innocent girl?"The debate also witnessed a heated exchange between Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and newly appointed Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi. The Wayanad MP alleged that Joshi had expressed "happiness" over the release of those convicted of raping a pregnant woman.While Priyanka Gandhi Vadra did not name the case, she appeared to be referring to the 2022 release of the 11 convicts in the Bilkis Bano gang-rape case. At the time, Joshi had said the release was in accordance with the law. The Supreme Court later quashed the remission and ordered the convicts back to prison in January 2024."The prime minister appointed a new education minister, a person who expressed consent and even happiness over the release of those convicted of raping a pregnant woman," the Wayanad MP alleged, prompting Joshi and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to intervene and demand that she substantiate the claim.An irate Joshi demanded that Priyanka Gandhi Vadra be expelled from the House and asked her to apologise for the remark.However, she hit back saying that has a video of the minister backing the convicted rapists."At a time when they are saying that they are bringing in women's rights, women's reservations and they are putting women in the forefront...It's a very wrong message...I am going to authenticate. There is a video of that time. I will submit everything with proper procedure," Priyanka Gandhi Vadra stated.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi backed his sister and remarked that there cannot a "filthier" person than one who defends release of convicted rapists."Education minister of India - the BJP puts a man who is a defender of rapists. That is the most filthy type of man. There can be no flithier man than somebody who says that rapists need protection. That is the education minister of India today. It's a strange reaction from the PM, that there are so many people in his cabinet, he could have chosen anyone of them. But he chooses a person who protects rapists. Quite amazing!," Rahul Gandhi told reporters.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha takes up Centre's proposed legislation to amend anti-paper leak law. Bill introduced on Monday after first week of Parliament's Monsoon session was washed out amid large-scale student protests. Opposition calls for tougher safeguards against examination fraud and wider education reforms following NEET (UG) question paper leak in May.

Article Title: PM Modi reviews Assam floods as over 4.45 lakh remain affected; Centre steps up relief
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday met members of parliament from Assam to review the state's flood situation, as the deluge continued to affect more than 4.45 lakh people across six districts, leaving a total of 631 villages currently underwater.Sharing details of the meeting on X, the Prime Minister said the Centre was working closely with the Assam government to support relief efforts."I pray for everyone's safety and well-being", the PM added.The meeting came as the flood situation in Assam's Sivasagar district continued to remain severe, with floodwaters entering homes and submerging roads in Naujan village. Hundreds of families have been left struggling for shelter, food and access to safe drinking water even as relief operations intensified.According to the latest bulletin issued by the Assam state disaster management authority (ASDMA), the number of people affected by the floods has declined to 4.45 lakh from over 5.24 lakh reported earlier. Officials quoted by news agency ANI said no fresh fatalities were reported, keeping the overall death toll at 68.The affected districts include Sivasagar, Golaghat, Charaideo, Jorhat, Nagaon and Kamrup (Metropolitan), with Charaideo remaining the worst-hit district, where around 1.88 lakh people continue to be affected.Sivasagar follows with 1.44 lakh affected residents, while Jorhat has reported 74,458 people impacted.According to ASDMA's Disaster Reporting and Information Management System, 631 villages across 21 revenue circles remain inundated.Officials said the Dhansiri (South) river was flowing above the danger level at Numaligarh in Golaghat district, while multiple agencies, including the National Disaster Response Force, State Disaster Response Force and civil defence personnel, continued rescue and relief operations.Authorities said 90 relief camps were operational, providing shelter to 28,695 displaced people, while another 94 relief distribution centres were supplying essential assistance.The floods have also affected agriculture, with 37,139.52 hectares of crop area remaining submerged. Officials said houses, roads and other public infrastructure had suffered damage across several affected districts.Meanwhile, Assam assembly Speaker Ranjeet Kumar Dass announced that all legislators, except those belonging to the Raijor Dal, would donate one month's salary towards flood relief and rehabilitation."Besides us, all Assembly secretariat staff will donate one day's salary for the relief and rehabilitation of the victims."Agriculture minister Pijush Hazarika welcomed the move, saying all Bharatiya Janata Party MLAs would also contribute one month's salary to the relief effort.A five-member central team led by ministry of home affairs joint secretary (disaster management) M Ramachandrudu visited Sivasagar on Monday to assess the flood situation in Upper Assam. State ministers Keshab Mahanta and Bimal Borah accompanied the delegation during the review.Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said power restoration was progressing as floodwaters receded."Since this morning, the number of families without power has declined by another 25 per cent. As floodwaters continue to recede, power supply is being restored across more affected areas. I will continue to share regular updates and keep you posted until power is restored to every affected household."Sarma also said the state had begun disinfection and fogging drives in flood-hit villages to prevent disease outbreaks as waters recede.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met members of parliament from Assam to review the state's flood situation. The deluge continued to affect more than 4.45 lakh people across six districts, leaving a total of 631 villages currently underwater. Hundreds of families have been left struggling for shelter, food and access to safe drinking water.

Article Title: Mekedatu row: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay writes to PM Modi; challenges Centre’s 'no consent needed' reply
Article Text:
File photo of Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi opposing Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu dam across the Cauvery and challenging the Centre’s claim that the consent of lower riparian states is not expressly required under the Supreme Court’s 2018 judgment.Vijay’s letter came a day after Union minister of state for Jal Shakti Raj Bhushan Choudhary told the Rajya Sabha that the February 16, 2018 verdict contained no provision requiring Karnataka to secure the approval of Tamil Nadu, Kerala or Puducherry before constructing a structure across the Cauvery. The reply was given to a question raised by PMK MP Anbumani Ramadoss."This disappointing reply from the Hon’ble Minister of State for Jal Shakti seems to have been made without taking into consideration the prevailing legal position and settled law with regard to the consent of the lower riparian states," Vijay said in his letter.The Tamil Nadu chief minister cited the Supreme Court’s ruling in the Alamatti dam dispute between Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh to argue that the consent of downstream states was necessary for projects capable of affecting river flows.Citing the judgment, Vijay said: "Nor can Karnataka State be permitted to construct up to that height without the consent of all other riparian States as well as without the approval of the Central government."He also referred to Clause XVIII of the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal’s final award, which preserves a state’s authority to regulate the use of water within its territory only when such action is not inconsistent with the tribunal’s order.Vijay argued that any project that could affect the regulated flow regime established under the award must therefore be examined for compliance with it.The Centre, in its Rajya Sabha reply, had relied on the same clause to say that the 2018 Supreme Court judgment did not specifically require Karnataka to obtain the consent of the other Cauvery basin states. It said states retained the authority to use water within their boundaries as long as their actions were not inconsistent with the tribunal’s directions.Tamil Nadu, however, maintained that the issue could not be decided merely by looking for an explicit consent clause in the 2018 verdict.In his letter, Vijay pointed to the tribunal’s directions concerning Kerala’s Pambar hydroelectric project, which involved only 0.1 TMC of consumptive use. The tribunal had directed Kerala and Tamil Nadu to jointly agree on the schedule of water releases to ensure that downstream irrigation was not adversely affected.According to Vijay, the direction showed that the tribunal had attached importance not only to annual water allocations but also to the coordinated regulation of releases affecting downstream states.He further cited Clause XI of the award, which, according to the letter, prohibits an upper riparian state from taking action affecting scheduled deliveries to downstream states except through mutual agreement and consultation with the regulatory authority.Clause XX, he said, recognises that changes to the award can be made only through an agreement among the party states."Tamil Nadu is therefore of the considered opinion that the proposed Mekedatu Project cannot be evaluated merely as an engineering proposal," Vijay wrote.He said the project’s legal permissibility must first be examined against the Cauvery tribunal’s final award, the Supreme Court’s February 2018 judgment and the rights of lower riparian states.The chief minister also pointed out that the Detailed Project Report submitted by Karnataka in 2019 had been returned by the Central Water Commission for revision to ensure compliance with the tribunal award and applicable guidelines.Tamil Nadu has consistently opposed Karnataka’s proposal to construct the balancing reservoir, arguing that it could affect the quantity and timing of Cauvery water reaching the downstream state.Karnataka maintains that the project is intended primarily to meet Bengaluru’s drinking-water requirements and generate hydroelectric power.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi opposing Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu dam across the Cauvery. Vijay’s letter came a day after Union minister of state for Jal Shakti Raj Bhushan Choudhary told the Rajya Sabha that the February 16, 2018 verdict contained no provision requiring Karnataka to secure approval.

Article Title: 'Fictional, unfounded': BJP dismisses report of portfolio change offer to Dharmendra Pradhan
Article Text:
Senior BJP leader Dharmendra Pradhan (PTI file photo)

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Sambit Patra on Tuesday dismissed reports claiming that the Centre had proposed a new ministerial portfolio for Dharmendra Pradhan after his resignation as Union education minister during talks with the Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ).The Puri MP and BJP leader said the reports had "no basis" and were published solely to "sensationalise the issue."Patra's clarification came after multiple media reports claimed that the Centre had discussed the possibility of assigning a new role to senior BJP leader Dharmendra Pradhan during negotiations with the CJP delegation.Addressing reporters, Patra said, "This morning, when I read the newspapers, I saw that a well-known and respected English-language newspaper had published a headline regarding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The report claimed that during negotiations between Union ministers Jp Nadda and Dr Jitendra Singh and representatives of the CJP, the central government proposed changing the education minister's portfolio and assigning him another ministry, with a new education minister set to take charge today. The newspaper further reported that the CJP objected to this proposal and, as a result, the respected minister had to resign."Patra, however, rejected the claim and said no such proposal had ever been discussed."Today, as the official spokesperson of the party, after reviewing the entire matter, I want to make it absolutely clear that this report published in a respected English newspaper is completely baseless.It is entirely fictional and unfounded. This news has no basis. It has no authenticity and has been published solely to sensationalise the issue," he said.After more than a month of protests at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar and demonstrations across the country over the NEET paper leak, Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister. Hours later, the CJP delegation called off its protest following multiple rounds of talks with Union ministers Jagat Prakash Nadda and Jitendra Singh.
Article Summary: BJP MP Sambit Patra dismisses reports claiming Centre proposed a new ministerial portfolio for Dharmendra Pradhan. Puri MP and BJP leader said the reports had "no basis" and were published solely to "sensationalise the issue"

Article Title: July 20 protest: RAF used tear gas, anti-riot guns and plastic pellets
Article Text:
Police record says RAF fired plastic pellets during July 20 NEET protest

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you believe was the main cause of the tensions during the protest? Police response Protester actions External influences Lack of communication 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Rapid Action Force personnel fired two rounds of non-lethal plastic pellets, along with tear smoke grenades and several other crowd-control munitions, during CJP's July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march over the NEET-UG paper leak, news agency PTI reported citing official records.The disclosure comes days after Delhi Police described allegations that pellets had been used against "peaceful protestors" as "completely false and misleading".According to officials, the details of the RAF action were entered in the general diary of Parliament Street police station on July 22, based on information provided by a deputy commandant of the force.The RAF unit was deployed in Zone 1 of the Jantar Mantar area alongside a Delhi Police officer of deputy commissioner of police rank.The police station record states that, acting on the DCP’s directions, RAF personnel fired 55 non-electrical shells, 15 electrical shells, five tear smoke grenades, two rounds from anti-riot guns and two rounds of plastic pellets while controlling the crowd on July 20.According to PTI, officials maintained that the plastic pellets used by the force were non-lethal and different from metal pellets that can penetrate the body.Each round contained four plastic pieces and was not expected to cause significant harm, they said.The use of pellets, however, has emerged as a source of controversy after protesters alleged that several participants suffered serious injuries during the march. The opposition has targeted the government over the police action and demanded a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah in Parliament.The protest was organised by the Cockroach Janta Party, which had been demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as education minister over the alleged leak of the NEET-UG question paper. Pradhan resigned on Saturday, following which the month-long agitation was called off.Multiple personnel from Delhi Police, the RAF and the Central Reserve Police Force were also injured during the protests. Several RAF personnel deployed in the Connaught Place area suffered injuries.The CRPF, under which the RAF operates, has now initiated a post-event assessment of the crowd-control operation. The review will examine the sequence of events, the circumstances in which different munitions were fired and whether the use of plastic pellets complied with established protocols.CRPF director General Gyanendra Pratap Singh said the force would arrive at an official view only after completing the assessment."Now, since agitation has been called off, and assembled people have dispersed, we would make a professional post-event assessment, like we do after every major assignment, and then let you know the view of the Force Hq (headquarters)," Singh said.Conducting such an assessment after a major deployment forms part of the CRPF’s standard operating procedure. Officials said the review would evaluate the RAF’s response as well as the wider operation undertaken to contain the march towards Parliament.A detailed report will be submitted to the force headquarters after the review is completed.Delhi Police and central forces had used tear gas, baton charges and other crowd-control measures after clashes broke out during the march. While several protesters alleged they suffered grievous pellet injuries, the police maintained that force was used to restore order after personnel were attacked.
Article Summary: RAF personnel fired two rounds of non-lethal plastic pellets, along with tear smoke grenades and several other crowd-control munitions. Delhi Police described allegations that pellets had been used against "peaceful protestors" as "completely false and misleading" The use of pellets has emerged as a source of controversy after protesters alleged that several participants suffered serious injuries.

Article Title: Bihar bandh violence: Siwan cop suspended for firing AK-47; 200 NEET protesters detained
Article Text:
Poll Vote & Share your view What is your opinion on the treatment of minors during detentions? It is unacceptable, they should be protected It's necessary for maintaining order 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PATNA: Nearly 200 students allegedly detained after the July 22 and 25 protests, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak, remained in custody for over 24 hours across police stations in the city, advocates alleged. Meanwhile, a Siwan police personnel was suspended for firing AK-47 during the July 25 bandh violence.Advocate Akanksha Shahi, who is providing legal aid to several detainees, said 58 of them were sent to remand on July 25. Around 87 more are likely to be sent to judicial custody on Sunday, she said. Several detainees are minors, she added.According to advocates, around 15 detainees were held at Gandhi Maidan police station, 28 at Digha, and 22 each at Rupaspura and Airport police stations, among others.Advocate Abhishek Kumar, who is also providing pro bono legal aid (free legal help), said the families of several detainees were not informed about their detention. He said detainees are required to be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours, which expired at 2pm on Sunday. The detainees were taken for medical examinations to govt hospitals around 5pm on Sunday, he said.Soma Kumari, a student activist and member of the Disha Students’ Organisation at Airport police station, said, “Over 200 people were detained during the July 25 protest.Around 70% of them are minors. Police are not informing us about the next step.”She added, “This is happening after it was assured by the govt that no action will be taken on the protesting students and all the FIRs will be quashed. But instead of quashing the FIRs, Patna police has kept them.”Families of the detainees said some students were caught while passing through the protest area.Shahi said the police were releasing all the women and minors, while other detainees were being sent to judicial custody.Responding to the allegations, Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma told TOI on Sunday that 86 protesters arrested during the July 25 violence near Gandhi Maidan were sent to judicial custody, while 60 others, including minors and women, were released on personal bonds. He said a case had been registered against the accused at Gandhi Maidan police station.The SSP added that in connection with the July 22 protest, police registered 23 FIRs across different police stations in the city and arrested 67 people, who were sent to judicial custody in different cases.Providing further details of the July 25 violence, Gandhi Maidan SHO Akhilesh Kumar Mishra, who sustained injuries during the clash, said four FIRs were registered in connection with the incident. One FIR was lodged on his statement, another on the statement of a magistrate, a third by the officer in charge of the Gandhi Maidan TOP checkpost that was attacked during the violence, and the fourth on a complaint by a repairman alleging that protesters overturned a govt vehicle parked near the police vehicle garage.Mishra said the accused have been booked under multiple charges, including unlawful assembly, rioting, attempt to murder, obstructing public servants from discharging their duties, and other offences related to the violence. Referring to the July 22 protest, Mishra said four FIRs were also registered at Gandhi Maidan police station, leading to the arrest of five people from the police station’s jurisdiction, while additional arrests were made by other police stations.Meanwhile, ADG (Law and Order) K Suhita Anupam said FIRs were registered in Saran, Siwan, Bhagalpur, Sitamarhi and Jehanabad in connection with violence during the July 25 bandh.She said 56 people were arrested in Saran, 25 in Siwan, 41 named accused in Bhagalpur, 13 in Sitamarhi and 13 in Jehanabad. She added that 19 govt vehicles and one private vehicle were vandalised, while 58 police personnel were injured, adding Siwan personnel who fired an AK-47 had been suspended.
Article Summary: Patna SSP Kartikeya K Sharma says 86 protesters arrested during the July 25 violence near Gandhi Maidan were sent to judicial custody. 60 others, including minors and women, were released on personal bonds. Siwan police personnel suspended for firing AK-47 during July 25 bandh violence.

Article Title: Did police arrest Warren Hudson in Nolan Wells death probe? Here’s what we know so far
Article Text:
Did police arrest Warren Hudson in Nolan Wells death probe? Here’s what we know so far (Image via Getty)

Was Nolan Wells friend Warren Hudson arrested?

What investigators have said about Nolan Wells before he disappeared?

The investigation into Mississippi teenager Nolan Wells’ death is still ongoing, but false claims continue to spread online. A Facebook post recently claimed that Wells’ friend, Warren Hudson, had been arrested in connection with the case. However, there is no evidence to support that claim. As of July 29, no one has been arrested, and Hudson has not been named a suspect by investigators. Officials are still waiting for the state coroner’s final findings and the toxicology report, while an independent autopsy has also failed to determine the exact cause of Wells’ death.The latest rumour started with a Facebook post shared by an account called RJ Haddy. The post claimed that a witness had provided a photo showing Warren Hudson attacking Nolan Wells with a rock. It added, “This detail may explain the abnormal mark on the back of Nolan’s head from the autopsy,” and included a video that appeared to show a teenager being arrested.There is no proof to support those claims. The video shared in the post is unrelated to the Nolan Wells case, and no law enforcement agency has announced Hudson’s arrest. Hudson was among the group of friends who were with Wells on Horn Island before he disappeared on July 4.He was also seen in the last known video of the group on a boat. Because he was one of the last people seen with Wells, investigators questioned him during the investigation. However, officials have not identified him as a suspect.Authorities have continued to say they currently suspect the death was an accident, and they have found no signs of foul play. Even so, the investigation remains open as officials wait for the remaining reports.The case also saw another update after ABC News, citing a witness account contained in a Mississippi Department of Marine Resources document, reported that Nolan Wells had consumed alcohol heavily before his death.An earlier document from the same agency said Wells stayed behind on Horn Island while the rest of the teenagers returned on the boat. According to the document, the group told investigators “that when they left he was in the company of an unknown female and that he chose to remain at the island.”That account has become an important part of the timeline, but officials have not linked it to any criminal activity. The state coroner’s final report and toxicology findings are still pending, and investigators have not announced any new suspects or arrests.For now, the viral claims about Warren Hudson being taken into custody remain false. The investigation into Nolan Wells’ death is continuing, and authorities have urged the public to rely on verified information instead of unconfirmed social media posts.
Article Summary: A Facebook post claimed that Wells’ friend, Warren Hudson, had been arrested in connection with the case. Hudson was among the group of friends who were with Wells on Horn Island before he disappeared on July 4. As of July 29, no one has been arrested, and Hudson has not been named a suspect by investigators.

Article Title: Kangana Ranaut fires fresh salvo at CJP's Saurav Das: Newton's 3rd law, 'useless' jibe, personal achievements; how feud escalated
Article Text:
A war of words has erupted between actor-turned-politician Kangana Ranaut and Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das.

Kangana Ranaut (Instagram Story)

Kangana calls protest videos 'puke inducing'

'Every action has equal and opposite reaction'

Saurav Das fires back

Kangana targets Saurav Das again





NEW DELHI: A war of words has erupted between actor-turned-politician Kangana Ranaut and Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das The row began after Ranaut launched a scathing attack on young people who participated in the CJP-led protests, branding Gen Z as "generation gutter" and describing videos from the demonstrations as "puke inducing".Her remarks quickly went viral, triggering criticism on social media and drawing a sharp response from Das, who said even members of her own party did not take her seriously.The exchange comes after the 36-day protest, led by the CJP along with students and civil society groups, ended on July 25 after the Centre accepted several key demands raised by the protesters, including the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, compensation for affected families and withdrawal of FIRs against protesters.BJP MP from Himachal Pradesh's Mandi launched a blistering attack on those who took part in the protests at Jantar Mantar."Never in my life I have seen so much ugliness in one place, these reels from GenZ protests are puke inducing, the way they speak and the kind of language they are using, never in my life I have seen everything in each and every frame so jarring and so crass all at ones, ewwww who is birthing and raising them?"She went on to accuse the protesters of tarnishing India's image."India is a place of diversely beautiful people, draped in elegance and rooted in cultural sophistication, you call yourself cockroaches and look/ behave like them as well there is no paradox or juxtaposition there, just simply subjecting the world to your filth, garbage and ugliness. I am scarred from these reels, need some healing, digital detox."Ranaut then turned her attention to women who had joined the demonstrations."Women who are truly independent they make rebellious choices, bold opinions, unconventional career moves and they take accountability for their actions. They have to cos they are on their own. They don't do this at the cost of their parents or families."Calling them "Generation gutter", she added, Here is a new generation of so called westernised Indian women. I call them Generation gutter."She further wrote, "They proudly flaunt their freedom to have drugs, drinks or endless body counts and shamelessly live off their patents earnings and constantly fight to live independent lives without actually being independent.""Gentle reminder independent life needs to be earned. If you try to live independently without accountability, you are just a distorted entity, gutter chaap."Ranaut defended criticism directed at protesters, saying those who publicly criticised the government should also be prepared to face backlash."Protestors who are getting beaten and abused on the roads by ordinary people because of their filthy and abusive reels must understand that if you speak, you also have to be prepared to listen. If you damage public property, then the public will damage you too."She added, "If you have a problem with the country and its leadership and have publicly hurled filthy abuses at them, then now listen to those who love this country and brought this government to power through their votes. Because they also have the right to speak."Invoking Newton's third law of motion, Ranaut concluded, "Every action has equal and opposite reaction. If studying hasn't helped you understand cause and effect, now you will understand it very well."Her remarks rapidly spread across social media, with many users criticising the actor-MP for what they described as "crass comments", while supporters defended her right to express her views.Das responded by dismissing Ranaut's criticism, saying her views carried little weight even within her own party."Even members of her own party don't pay much heed to Kangana Ranaut or take her seriously, so why should we? I don't think anyone in Gen Z, Gen Alpha, or any younger generation takes her seriously or listens to what she says. She is a politician now."He also referred to comments Ranaut had previously made about the workload of being a Member of Parliament."There were videos from when she visited her constituency in Himachal Pradesh where she remarked that she had expected the job to require very little work, only to realise that being a Member of Parliament involves a massive amount of labour. That speaks volumes about her own seriousness."The confrontation escalated on Tuesday when Ranaut singled out CJP leader Saurav Das after sharing a screenshot of his ANI interview on Instagram stories.Questioning his identity as a student, she wrote, "Googled this person and he is 28 years old, how he claims to be a student I have no clue!! Yes I am in politics for past 2 years but I have been in public life for last 20 years."She then compared his life with her own achievements, "At his age I had 2 National Awards, yes as a new parliamentarian I was overwhelmed with all the work because I am also a filmmaker + performing artist + producer + screen writer + entrepreneur."Ranaut continued, "But someone like him who is totally useless and unemployed will never understand what it means to be in massive demand and at all times at any age."Addressing Das directly, she added, "Dear Saurav your issues are personal, you are not a student you are simply useless, let’s start with learning some skill. It’s a good place to start."
Article Summary: Kangana Ranaut launches scathing attack on young people who participated in the CJP-led protests. She brands Gen Z as "generation gutter" and describes videos from the demonstrations as "puke inducing" Her remarks quickly went viral, triggering criticism on social media and drawing a sharp response from Saurav Das.

Article Title: Gone in 16 days: Dehradun’s Rs 16 crore bridge collapses in rain
Article Text:
The bridge, inaugurated on July 12, was built to replace the previous structure that was washed away in Sept last year, killing 14 people

Poll Vote & Share your view What should be the top focus to prevent infrastructure failures? Better construction standards Regular safety inspections 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





DEHRADUN: Just 17 days after it was opened to traffic, the Rs 16-crore bridge at Nanda ki Chowki in Dehradun became the latest casualty of heavy rainfall after a large section of its approach road collapsed early Tuesday, leaving a gaping crater that disconnected the bridge from the Dehradun-Paonta Sahib highway. Officials, however, maintained that the “bridge itself remains structurally safe” and that only the approach road collapsed after overnight rain washed away the soil beneath it.The bridge, inaugurated on July 12 after missing its original April 30 deadline, was built to replace the previous structure that was washed away in Sept last year, killing 14 people.The incident prompted district magistrate Ashish Chauhan to take cognisance of the collapse and direct officials to take action against those found responsible if lapses in construction or execution are established.PWD secretary Pankaj Kumar Pandey said, “The chief engineer of the regional office has been directed to investigate the cause of the incident, fix responsibility and submit a report, along with all supporting evidence, to the govt within three days. If the preliminary inquiry finds negligence on the part of officials or contractors, appropriate action will be taken. Any delay is unacceptable. Restoring the road is the department’s top priority.The cave-in disrupted traffic between Dehradun, Vikasnagar and neighbouring Himachal Pradesh, with vehicles being diverted via Jhajhra on the outskirts of Dehradun. “We are waiting for the Tons River’s water level to recede before soil filling can be undertaken safely and traffic can be restored,” district disaster management officer Rishabh Kumar said.Officials from the irrigation department have also been deployed at the site to regulate the flow of the river and prevent further damage.The bridge-collapse sparked sharp criticism from residents and the opposition, with questions being raised over quality of construction despite the hefty cost involved.“Authorities are doing nothing but evading accountability... It took almost a year for the bridge to be completed. The govt spent Rs 16 crore on it and within days such a huge sinkhole appeared. The public is angry over such poor-quality infrastructure. Shouldn’t the PWD minister be held accountable?“ asked social activist Anoop Nautiyal.Meanwhile, the district administration said “temporary repairs had been carried out and traffic restored”. Following directions from the CM, clarifications were sought from the concerned officials and contractor. District magistrate Ashish Chauhan subsequently ordered action against those found responsible.
Article Summary: The Rs 16-crore bridge at Nanda ki Chowki in Dehradun became the latest casualty of heavy rainfall. A large section of its approach road collapsed early Tuesday, leaving a gaping crater. Officials, however, maintained that the “bridge itself remains structurally safe’ The bridge was built to replace the previous structure that was washed away in Sept last year, killing 14 people.

Article Title: US envoy Gor to visit Bangladesh as Dhaka deepens ties with Beijing
Article Text:
File photo: US Envoy Sergio Gor

DHAKA: US's special envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor is scheduled to visit Bangladesh on July 30 - the first by a senior US diplomat after PM Tarique Rahman's June tour of China and amid Dhaka's strong engagements in various fields, including trade, economic corridor and defence, with Beijing.Gor, who is also US ambassador to India, will meet PM Tarique and foreign minister Khalilur Rahman apart from his other engagements in Dhaka, diplomatic sources said. "The relationship between Bangladesh and the US has always been good, and that relationship is getting stronger under the current govt," said state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam recently, hoping the visit will bring a new dimension to relations between the two countries.Sources said the visit aims at giving the US a "clear understanding" of Bangladesh's foreign policy priorities, as Washington remains "concerned" over Beijing's proposal to have an economic corridor connecting Bangladesh and Myanmar.
Article Summary: US's special envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor is scheduled to visit Bangladesh on July 30. It is the first by a senior US diplomat after PM Tarique Rahman's June tour of China. The visit aims at giving the US a "clear understanding" of Bangladesh's foreign policy priorities.

Article Title: Oman proposes Gulf-backed voluntary fees to use Hormuz
Article Text:
File photo: Ships in Hormuz

DUBAI: Oman has presented Iran with a plan backed by Gulf states to manage the Strait of Hormuz, including collecting voluntary fees for using it, a Gulf source and a Western diplomat told Reuters on Tuesday. A senior Iranian source told Reuters that Tehran was yet to respond to the Omani proposals, intended to serve as a basis to end the disruption to trade through the strait caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran.President Donald Trump, who abruptly called off a two-week US bombing campaign over the weekend in his latest strategic U-turn, said there were "good talks" under way with Iran but threatened to restart strikes unless negotiations deliver. Iran denies seeking to resume talks with the US. Washington launched its renewed bombing campaign earlier this month to break Iran's grip on the strait.Iran effectively shut the strait to ships other than its own after the US and Israel attacked on Feb 28. A deal last month between the US and Iran partially reopened it, but the agreement collapsed in early July after Iran fired on ships using a channel it does not approve.Iran has said it wants to manage the strait alongside Oman, which controls the opposite shore, and charge service fees to ships that use it. Washington wants to return to the status quo prior to the war, when ships were able to pass freely with no payments, and says charging mandatory fees would be illegal.Under the Omani proposal, Iran would not exercise sole control and fees would be voluntary, the Gulf source and Western diplomat briefed on the matter told Reuters. The system would be analogous to one in place on Asia's Strait of Malacca, where Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore ask ships to pay voluntary contributions to fund navigation, environmental protection and search-and-rescue operations.The Western diplomat compared it to a voluntary carbon tax for flights, where anyone buying a plane ticket can choose to tick a box if they want to pay to offset their emissions. Gulf Cooperation Council foreign ministers met via video call on Tuesday to discuss the latest developments in the conflict, including ways to intensify cooperation on issues related to freedom and safety of vessels through the waterway, a statement from the Qatari foreign ministry said.Iran's joint military command again rejected a plan put forward by Trump for damages to vessels to be paid from frozen Iranian assets, state media reported. It said that any country or company that accepted such payments would be denied passage through the Strait of Hormuz by Iran's armed forces.(BY REUTERS)
Article Summary: Oman has presented Iran with a plan backed by Gulf states to manage the Strait of Hormuz. The plan includes collecting voluntary fees for using it, a Gulf source and a Western diplomat said. Washington launched its renewed bombing campaign earlier this month to break Iran's grip on the strait.

Article Title: Middle East war escalates: Multiple dead in US-Saudi strikes in Iraq; Iran targets Hormuz ships - top developments
Article Text:
US-Saudi hit Iran-linked entities in Iraq; Tehran hits US bases, ships in Hormuz

US, Saudi Arabia strike Iran-backed groups in Iraq

Iran denies role in Saudi drone attacks

Eight Iraqi PMF members killed

US says it intercepted Iranian missiles

Iran hits US bases in Jordan, claims it stopped 3 oil tankers in Hormuz

Oil prices rise as diplomatic efforts continue

The war in the Middle East escalated once again after couple of days of fragile peace as the United States and Saudi Arabia launched joint strikes on Iran-backed armed groups in Iraq on Wednesday. Meanwhile, Iran claimed to have intercepted oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and fired missiles at US military installations.Washington said the strikes targeted logistics and weapons sites used by Iran-backed militias to launch more than 30 drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities over the past 72 hours. The operation came hours after US Central Command (CENTCOM) said it had intercepted all Iranian ballistic missiles fired at American forces in the Middle East.The latest exchanges have renewed fears of a wider regional conflict centred on the Strait of Hormuz, the strategic waterway that normally carries about 20 per cent of the world's traded oil.The US and Saudi Arabia said they struck multiple sites across eastern Iraq used by Iran-backed militias to direct drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure.CENTCOM warned that the Revolutionary Guard and its allied groups "must cease these attacks to avoid further US military response."Saudi Arabia said it does not seek escalation but would respond to any aggression targeting the kingdom.Iran rejected allegations that it directed recent drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities.An Iranian defence official described attempts to link Tehran to attacks on US interests and Saudi targets as a "major miscalculation."Iraqi militias also denied responsibility, while the Iran-backed Islamic Resistance in Iraq suggested Houthi rebels in Yemen were behind the attacks.Iraq's Popular Mobilisation Forces (PMF) said several of its headquarters were hit in the strikes.The PMF's Nineveh command said eight of its members were killed and four others wounded in the joint US-Saudi attacks in the northern Iraqi province, as reported by Al Jazeera.Flames and thick plumes of smoke rising from sites in Iraq's northern Nineveh province and southern Basra province following the joint US-Saudi strikes. The circulating footage also showed firefighters arriving at one of the targeted locations in Basra.Earlier, CENTCOM said it intercepted all ballistic missiles launched by Iran in what it described as an attempted surprise attack on US forces in the Middle East.Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), meanwhile, said it had fired ballistic missiles at US military installations in Jordan, while vowing to continue responding to what it called unlawful US actions.Iran launched a barrage of ballistic missiles targeting US forces in Jordan after a five-day pause in hostilities, prompting the US military to intercept all incoming projectiles, according to US Central Command (CENTCOM).The attack coincided with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's visit to the White House, marking a renewed escalation in the conflict after several days of relative calm.The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said its naval forces struck and stopped three oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz after they ignored warnings and sailed along what it called an "unsafe and illegal route."It warned that any vessel following "unlawful US military interference" or instructions in the strategic waterway would "not go unanswered." Reuters could not independently verify the claim.Oil prices climbed more than $3 a barrel amid concerns that renewed fighting could further disrupt energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz.Separately, Oman has proposed a Gulf-backed framework for jointly managing navigation through the strait, while the US reiterated that the international waterway should remain free from Iranian control or restrictions.The renewed fighting comes after a short-lived lull in hostilities and as President Donald Trump warned Iran that the US would "finish the job" if Tehran failed to reach a deal to end the conflict. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also met Trump at the White House on Tuesday, with both leaders describing the talks as productive.
Article Summary: US, Saudi Arabia strike Iran-backed groups in Iraq. Iran claims to have intercepted oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran denies role in Saudi drone attacks on oil facilities. US Central Command says it intercepted all Iranian ballistic missiles fired at American forces.

Article Title: CJP protest in Mumbai: Cop ‘inappropriately touches’ woman in video, stirs row
Article Text:
The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.





MUMBAI: A viral video from the CJP protest at Shivaji Park on Thursday, showing a policeman allegedly inappropriately touching a woman protester, stirred up a fresh controversy on Friday, with the opposition demanding his dismissal.The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage.DCP (operations) Akbar Pathan said, “The official was trying to hold on to a male protester and a lady stepped in while he was looking away. Senior officers have verified all the facts and minutely assessed the video to ascertain the facts,” he said.Another police official said, “Since the video went viral late Thursday night, our senior cyber crime experts carefully zoomed in on the footage, verified it, and found that there was no misconduct.”The controversy came a day after another viral video showed a police constable, who was working as a driver, allegedly threatening young protesters that drugs would be planted on them and their career would be ruined if they continued participating in protests.The latest video quickly went viral on social media, with several opposition politicians demanding action against the policeman. Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal demanded an apology from CM Devendra Fadnavis and dismissal of the policeman.In a post on X, Sapkal said, “The one who calls himself Devabhaau has turned out to be Duryodhan! Devabhaau’s police have become so rogue that they are violating the modesty of female students the age of their own daughters.”Mumbai Congress president and MP Varsha Gaikwad said, “What happened to a girl during the protest in Mumbai is deeply painful and disturbing. It is wrong to speak of the ‘Ladki Bahin’ scheme while treating young women in such a manner. It is a matter of shame that women are allegedly being mistreated in the land of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. False cases are being registered against students, and they are being threatened. ”Congress has organised statewide candlelight marches and ‘satyagraha’ in Maharashtra on Saturday to express solidarity with the protesting students.
Article Summary: The police, however, dismissed the charges levelled against the policeman, saying there was no act of misconduct by the officer seen in the footage. The controversy came a day after another viral video showed a police constable, who was working as a driver, allegedly threatening young protesters.

Article Title: 3 years on, SIT probe complete in just 10% of Manipur riot cases
Article Text: NEW DELHI: More than three years after Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives, Supreme Court was informed Friday that probes into only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by SITs of state police while CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.Appearing for the CBI, additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that the central probe agency had filed chargesheets in 21 cases and closure reports in six, of which three had been accepted. It was continuing investigations into the remaining four cases.Former Maharashtra DGP Dattatray Padsalgikar, who was appointed to oversee the investigations, informed the court through a report that of the 3,020 cases being probed by the SITs across eight districts, chargesheets had been filed in only 301 cases and trial had commenced in 10.The CJI-led bench told the investigators to act expeditiously. Given the volume of cases, SC mulled setting up special courts to try these exclusively. It sought responses to this from Manipur govt and the high courts of Assam and Manipur.SC had transferred investigations into cases of rape-murder other heinous offence to CBI and shifted their trial to Guwahati. The central agency told the court that examination of witnesses residing in Manipur through video-conferencing was a challenge because of law-and-order situations, non-cooperation and language barriers as they spoke different dialects.Senior advocate Ngangom Junior Luwang complained that no effort had been made to trace 30 missing people and without their remains, authorities were not issuing death certificates required for other purposes. SC asked him to approach Manipur high court.Advocate Sharukh Alam submitted that land belonging to churches vandalised during the clashes were getting encroached upon and said govt had taken no steps to reconstruct them. Bhati said govt's priority was to reconstruct damaged dwelling units. The bench said govt was right to prioritise reconstructing houses but asked it to take steps to stop encroachment of places of worship.
Article Summary: Kuki-Meitei ethnic clashes singed Manipur and claimed 260 lives. Only 10% of the 3,000-odd cases had been completed by state police. CBI had investigated the majority of the 31 cases referred to it.

Article Title: 'Ab aayega aur maza!' CJP says 'time is ticking' as farmers announce march to Jantar Mantar on Sunday

CJP's Saurav Das alleges tanks being transported to Delhi

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokesperson Saurav Das on Saturday urged the Centre to accept the protesters' demands, alleging that the government was transporting tanks to Delhi while the student agitation continued."Ab aayega aur maza! The government must understand that it can either bomb the peaceful protesters using the tanks it is transporting to Delhi (I mean, what are they trying to do by transporting these? Kill their own children? Is this where we have come in Gandhi's India?) Or, accept demands. The time is ticking!" Das said in a post on X.He made the remarks while sharing a post by the Bharatiya Kisan Union announcing that it would join the ongoing student protest at Jantar Mantar.The development comes as CJP reiterated that it may adopt a "tough stance" if the Centre does not clarify its position on the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.Speaking to reporters, CJP activist Ashutosh Ranka said the meeting with Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh was constructive, but added that the organisation was still awaiting the government's response to its primary demand."Yesterday's meeting yielded a positive response regarding compensation and legal matters, reaching an in-principle agreement. Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation.""Mainstream media reports suggest sources are saying Pradhan will not step down. If he does not resign, the government should state it clearly, as there is no point in continuing these meetings. We will then decide on our next steps. If the government continues this approach, we will be forced to take a tough stance," Ranka said.Earlier, activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh after the Union government gave a written assurance on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.Meanwhile, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said strict action would be taken against those responsible for the alleged paper leaks. Article Title: 'All out of control': Spain invokes first wildfire emergency as fires rage across Europe; over 10,000 evacuated
Article Text:
A wall of flames advances as a wildfire burns near Burgohondo, in Ávila province, Spain (Picture credit: AP)

First wildfire emergency in Spain

France asks EU for firefighting aircraft

Poll Vote & Share your view How concerned are you about the increasing intensity of wildfires in southern Europe? Very concerned Not concerned at all 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Heatwave and climate concerns

Spain declared a national emergency over wildfires for the first time on Friday, while France requested European Union assistance to battle a major blaze on its Atlantic coast, as an intense heatwave drove destructive fires across southern Europe and forced the evacuation of tens of thousands of people.The emergency declaration in Spain followed multiple uncontrolled fires around Madrid and in neighbouring Ávila province, prompting authorities to evacuate more than 10,000 residents from towns in the mountains west of the capital.The measure allows Spain's interior ministry to take charge of coordinating firefighting operations nationwide.French authorities ordered the full evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula, a popular tourist destination near Bordeaux, where around 40,000 people were forced to leave campsites, holiday homes and residential areas, with many evacuated by boat.Spanish officials said this was the first time the country had activated its highest level of emergency specifically for a wildfire. The same level had previously been used during a nationwide power blackout last year.More than 270 emergency personnel, 40 ground units and several contingents from Spain's Military Emergency Unit have been deployed to the affected areas.In Navaluenga, one of the worst-hit towns in Ávila province, residents watched helicopters scoop water from the local river as smoke filled the air."I've lived here for 36 years and I've never seen anything like it. Nor did I expect it. I thought they were going to get it under control last night, but it was already late, and it was all out of control," resident Javier Martin told Reuters.According to the EU's European Forest Fire Information Service (EFFIS), more than 350 fires have burned in Spain so far this year. About 1,300 square kilometres have already been destroyed, more than four times the area burned during the same period last year.Spain has also suffered its second-largest wildfire on record this year, which burned roughly 320 square kilometres in Guadalajara province north of Madrid.Earlier this month, 13 people were killed in a fire in southern Spain, the country's deadliest wildfire in recent memory.The Cap Ferret fire has already burned about 8,700 hectares, or 87 square kilometres, making it one of France's most serious blazes in recent years.President Emmanuel Macron announced that France had activated the EU Civil Protection Mechanism and requested additional firefighting resources from European partners."France has requested the activation of the European Union's civil protection mechanism," Macron wrote on X, adding that specialist aircraft from several European countries were expected to arrive soon.The EU is sending two Croatian Canadair firefighting planes, two Portuguese Air Tractor aircraft and heavy-lift Black Hawk helicopters from the Czech Republic and Slovakia.The blaze has spread through pine forests near Bordeaux's wine-growing region, turning the sky orange and filling nearby areas with smoke.Residents described hurried evacuations as flames approached homes."The gendarmes came and knocked on every door, the fire was about 500 metres away -- we grabbed some things and left," Patrick Martineau, a resident of Le Porge, told news agency AFP.Temperatures are expected to exceed 39°C in parts of southeastern Spain, with some areas forecast to reach 44°C.Smoke from the fires was reportedly noticeable in parts of Madrid on Friday morning.The crisis is part of a broader pattern of increasingly severe wildfires across southern Europe. EFFIS satellite data show that the total area burned across EU countries this year is already the second-largest on record.Europe is warming roughly twice as fast as the global average, according to the EU's Copernicus Climate Change Service. Scientists say human-caused climate change is intensifying heatwaves and drought conditions, making the region more vulnerable to large, fast-moving fires.Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called the situation "dramatic" and renewed his appeal for a political pact to tackle climate change, saying the country must adapt to a future of more frequent and intense wildfires.The fires have also taken a heavy toll on emergency responders.Three firefighters have died during wildfire operations in southern Europe in recent days, including two who were killed while battling a blaze near Bordeaux airport earlier this week.
Article Summary: Spain declares national emergency over wildfires for the first time. France requests EU assistance to battle a major blaze on its Atlantic coast. More than 350 fires have burned in Spain so far this year, more than four times the area burned in the same period last year.

Article Title: US man gets two life terms for killing ex-Minnesota lawmaker Melissa Hortman, husband
Article Text:
Pictures of Mark and Melissa Hortman inside the sanctuary at the Basilica of St. Mary's during their funeral (Photo: AP).

A US District Court on Thursday sentenced Vance Boelter to two consecutive life terms plus 40 years in prison for the fatal shooting of former Minnesota Democratic lawmaker Melissa Hortman and her husband, Mark Hortman, in a politically motivated attack.Boelter was also convicted of critically injuring state senator John Hoffman and his wife, Yvette, along with two counts of attempted murder, impersonating a police officer and animal cruelty.Nearly a year after the Minneapolis-area attacks, Boelter agreed to plead guilty in June for fear of federal prosecutors seeking the death penalty.On June 14, 2025, Vance Boelter reportedly rang the doorbell to Hortman’s home at around 3:30 am, disguised as a police officer on a welfare check, wearing a uniform and a mask.Once Mark Hortman answered the door, Boelter gave him a fake name and badge number before requesting him to summon Melissa Hortman, following which he killed both of them, shooting multiple times.According to police, Boelter had already visited the Hoffmans’, shooting and critically injuring the senator and his wife. In failed attempts, he reportedly also went to two other lawmakers’ houses that night.“My days are filled with grey, and the blood that was spilt is the last thing I see before I go to sleep and the first thing I see when I wake,” said Colin, son of the Hortmans, while speaking to CNN“There is no sentence that weighs 15 gunshots, a murdered dog and the rest of my life”, he added.Speaking to CNN, state senator John Hoffman shared what he experienced on the night of the incident.“The defendant looked me in the eyes and pulled the trigger. The defendant looked at my wife and chose to do the same,” Hoffman said, adding that he and his wife now live with the injuries, with their bodies remembering the gunfire.According to CNN, Boelter admitted to identifying and stalking his targets for months before carrying out the attacks.
Article Summary: Vance Boelter sentenced to two consecutive life terms plus 40 years in prison. Former Minnesota Democratic lawmaker Melissa Hortman and her husband, Mark Hortman, were killed in a politically motivated attack.Boelter also convicted of critically injuring state senator John Hoffman and his wife, Yvette, along with two counts of attempted murder.
